gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Wide openings on small letters and a pronounced x-height make Noto Sans Arabic easy to settle into. Visitor adds a nostalgic digital punch up top, every stroke piped out like solder through a nozzle, and that is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Visitor cuts every stroke end as if from one ribbon, a nostalgic, digital look with gaping mouths on its e. Yet Noto Sans Armenian below keeps its round letters wide and inviting, so a long passage goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Visitor brings a nostalgic, digital feel, with no calligraphic shading to steer the eye and short ascenders over big bowls. And Noto Sans Avestan follows with curves whose tips never touch and a pronounced x-height, a clean modern counterweight on the page.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-batak: Marker-drawn plainness runs through every character of Visitor, giving it a nostalgic, digital edge with short ascenders over big bowls. But Noto Sans Batak keeps a stubby, towering x-height and an e that never squeezes shut, so a longer read stays smooth.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cham: Retro and wiry, with a rope-thin outline in Visitor that never swells or thins, then a body font with open c shapes and rounded, lofty lowercase. Visitor is best at bold display moments; Noto Sans Cham handles the steady reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Blocky, nostalgic and digital, Visitor drops every swing between thick and thin, with short ascenders over big bowls. Noto Sans Cherokee follows with a lofty band of letters and an e with a wide gap at its terminal, so a longer passage moves along easily.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-devanaga: Noto Sans Devanagari is a modern, neutral sans with an open-curved g and capitals that blend into a compact skyline. Visitor, with no hairlines to squint at in small sizes, adds a nostalgic digital bite, and that crisp difference is what makes this pairing click.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Visitor looks drawn with a single pen tip, nostalgic and digital, with short ascenders sitting above big bowls and gaping mouths on the e. Noto Sans Elymaic follows with open apertures throughout, so a longer passage reads cleanly.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Marker-nib scrawl meets sturdy order, since Visitor ignores direction in its line while Noto Sans Ethiopic hangs its c terminals far from the bowl. Visitor is at home when it is big and short.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Visitor runs a single flat line weight through every glyph, a nostalgic, digital look with short ascenders over big bowls. Give Noto Sans Grantha a little extra size, since its small letters sit like flattened pen-nib bowls.
